topic: Android interview: lifecycle, config changes & process death

questions.question: The user rotates the device. The Activity does not declare android:configChanges. What happens by default?
options: The Activity is only paused and resumed; onCreate is not called again
The Activity and all its ViewModels are rebuilt from scratch
The Activity is destroyed and recreated, while its ViewModels are kept
Only the window is redrawn with the new resources, nothing is recreated
questions.explanation: A configuration change destroys and recreates the Activity so new resources are loaded, but the ViewModelStore is retained across the change, so ViewModels survive. Saying ViewModels are rebuilt confuses a config change with the Activity finishing.

questions.question: A ViewModel's in-memory fields survive when the system kills the app process in the background and the user later returns to it.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: A ViewModel lives in process memory, so system-initiated process death wipes it. Only state written into saved instance state (for example via SavedStateHandle) is handed back to the new process; the ViewModel itself is constructed fresh.

questions.question: Activity A starts Activity B, which fully covers it. In what order do the lifecycle callbacks run?
options: A.onPause, B.onCreate, B.onStart, B.onResume, A.onStop
A.onPause, A.onStop, B.onCreate, B.onStart, B.onResume
B.onCreate, B.onStart, B.onResume, A.onPause, A.onStop
A.onStop, A.onPause, B.onCreate, B.onStart, B.onResume
questions.explanation: A is paused first, then B goes all the way to resumed, and only once B is visible does A get onStop. This is why heavy work in onPause delays the next screen, and why you should not assume A is stopped before B starts.

questions.question: The system kills your process while it is in the background, then the user returns via Recents. Which of these are restored? Select all that apply.
options: Values written to a ViewModel's SavedStateHandle
A Kotlin object singleton's cached user profile
The task's stack of Activities, recreated as needed
Data put into the onSaveInstanceState Bundle
Fields held directly in a ViewModel instance
questions.explanation: The system keeps the task's activity records and their saved Bundles (SavedStateHandle data is stored in that Bundle), and recreates Activities from them. Anything that only lived in process memory, such as singletons and ViewModel fields, starts over from its initial value.

questions.question: For apps targeting API 28 and above, when is onSaveInstanceState called relative to the other callbacks as an Activity goes to the background?
options: Before onPause, so state is captured while the UI is still interactive
After onStop, once the Activity is no longer visible
Between onPause and onStop, always in that exact slot
Only in onDestroy, and only if the process is about to be killed
questions.explanation: Since API 28, onSaveInstanceState runs after onStop. Before that it ran before onStop with no guarantee relative to onPause. It is not tied to onDestroy: it runs whenever the Activity may later need recreating, whether or not the process actually dies.

questions.question: Why is the 'Don't keep activities' developer option not a faithful simulation of process death?
options: It never triggers onSaveInstanceState, so nothing is restored
It also clears the saved Bundle, so it is stricter than real death
It keeps ViewModels alive, hiding bugs in SavedStateHandle usage
The process stays alive, so singletons and statics keep their values
questions.explanation: 'Don't keep activities' destroys each Activity as you leave it, but the process lives on, so in-memory singletons, caches and static fields survive and can mask bugs. ViewModels are cleared in that mode because the destroy isn't a config change. To truly test, background the app and run `adb shell am kill <package>`.

questions.question: If the user explicitly swipes the task away from the Recents screen, the saved instance state is discarded and the next launch starts fresh.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Saved instance state is meant for system-initiated destruction. When the user deliberately dismisses the task, Android treats it as the user being done with it, so the saved Bundles go away. Data that must survive this belongs in persistent storage such as DataStore or a database.

questions.question: On Android 7+ an app puts a ~2 MB list into onSaveInstanceState. What happens when the Activity is stopped?
options: The excess is silently truncated and the list restores partially
The Bundle is written to disk because it exceeds the binder limit
A TransactionTooLargeException crashes the app
Only a warning is logged and the state is dropped without a crash
questions.explanation: The saved Bundle travels to system_server over Binder, whose transaction buffer is about 1 MB shared by the process. Since API 24 going over it throws TransactionTooLargeException instead of failing quietly. Keep saved state small: IDs and user input, not loaded data.

questions.question: Without any android:configChanges declared, which of these recreate a running Activity? Select all that apply.
options: The user switches the system to dark theme
The device connects to a different Wi-Fi network
The user changes the system language
A notification arrives in the status bar
The app window is resized in multi-window mode
questions.explanation: uiMode (dark theme), locale and screen size changes are configuration changes, so the Activity is recreated to reload resources. Connectivity changes and notifications don't alter the Configuration, so they don't recreate anything. Forgetting that dark mode and multi-window recreate the Activity is a common source of lost state.

questions.question: An Activity declares android:configChanges="orientation|screenSize". What happens on rotation?
options: It is not recreated; onConfigurationChanged gets the new Configuration
It is recreated as usual, but onCreate receives a null Bundle
Rotation is blocked and the screen stays in its current orientation
It is recreated, but its Views are kept and re-attached automatically
questions.explanation: Declaring the change means the Activity handles it itself: it stays alive and onConfigurationChanged is called. Resources are not reloaded for you, so you must update anything orientation-dependent. It does not lock orientation; that is screenOrientation.
